evidence.baseline: Security is never absolute; it is always a relationship between the cost of defense and the value of attack. The relevant question is not whether a system can be broken by the most capable adversary on Earth. It is whether the safeguards are strong enough that, for the overwhelming majority of people and the overwhelming majority of threats, the system is genuinely trustworthy.
evidence.shipped: Security must begin with a threat model. Protection suitable for ordinary commercial tracking may be inadequate for activists, journalists, survivors, dissidents, or people targeted by a state.

evidence.baseline: It defeats the commercial surveillance that is the actual, present, mass-scale threat (the harvesting and monetization of intimate signal by corporations) completely, because there is no cloud to harvest from and no closed code in which to hide the harvesting.
evidence.shipped: Metadata can reveal relationships even when content remains private.

findings.diagnosis: Completely is falsified by traffic analysis: even a cloudless federated network exposes who attests with whom and when, unless the protocol hides it. The shipped sentence names that residue in seven words. Kept verbatim directly after the completeness claim, where it converts an absolute into an honest bound without softening the genuine advantage. The shipped per-population threat-model paragraph (activists, journalists, survivors, dissidents) and the recovery-and-coercion sentence are preserved here for CTD-0027's threat-model design, with the humility-to-tell-some-users sentence flagged as an adoption candidate: the current tool cannot safely serve them is a commitment the baseline never makes and should.
